**decision: a block-sparse tile kernel of our own on joint_matrix, borrowing chunk_prefill's structure (both GEMMs

sequence's pages in 8-page (32-key) steps, skips a step no row of the tile selects, stages K^T / V once per step for
the 64 rows, membership from a per-row bitmap over page indices (to be written by the select kernel beside its
page-id list, since the list holds page ids in radix order and no inverse map exists on the device), causality by
key position. Expected: the staging amortised over 64 rows instead of 1, the DPAS work at 64 x 32 tiles, the
skipped steps giving the union's cost: attention 1.77 s -> ~0.2-0.4 s of the 7K (−13 %) and more at 20K |
alternative: port chunk_prefill as is and run it dense-causal on each chunk, masking nothing (wrong: the model
would attend to unselected pages beyond 2,051 tokens -- a different function, not a form) | why: the selection is
the model; only a kernel that honours per-row lists is a form of it.** Step 1 this run (no arch change yet): the
standalone probe probe2/attn_tile_probe.cpp (synthetic rows: all pages below 2,051, the 64 local + 448 random pages

- **The integration design (next run; settled this run):** everything stays in libxe plus one op row -- the
  select kernel and its bytes are untouched. A new op `attn_qsa_fmha` for one-sequence sparse prefill passes
  of >= 256 rows: operands q [T][heads x 256] bf16, the kv cache, `sel` [T][topk + 1] and `nsel` [T] (the lists
  as they are), the sequence's block table [1][max_blocks] and its context length, out; the rows' positions are
  ctx − T + i (a chunk is consecutive). Scratch: (1) an inverse map page id -> block index for the sequence
  (num_blocks x i32, filled by a kernel from the table: no inverse exists today, and the lists hold page ids in
  radix order); (2) the per-row bitmap over block indices [T padded to 256][ceil(pages/32)] u32, filled by a
  kernel from sel / nsel through the inverse (the partial page included); (3) the context's K and V gathered from
  the 4-token E4M3 pages into dense [ctx][256] buffers (fp16 or bf16: E4M3 exact in both; ~1 KB a token, 16 MB a
  layer at 16K); then the FMHA kernel (sycl-tla's mainloop with the mask, the example's kernel / epilogue /
  scheduler, head-256 policy, causal, seq_len_qo = T over seq_len_kv = ctx) writing out directly. Build: the
  sycl-tla headers from third_party/ (header-only, pinned) plus the mask-patched mainloop copied under
  src/libxe/fmha/ with its BSD-3 notice; the extra link flags (-Xspirv-translator -spirv-ext=+split_barrier,
  +2d_block_io,+subgroup_matrix_multiply_accumulate) are harmless for the other kernels but the CPU device cannot
  run 2D block loads, so the op is GPU-only (RAD_E_DEVICE elsewhere) and its CPU-side tests cover the three prep
  kernels only; the FMHA's check is the card test (the probe's host reference) and the engine's KL replay.
  Dispatch in the arch's sparse branch (rad_block_attn_gated_fp8.h:580-594): when the step is one sequence and T
  >= 256 and the op resolved, issue it once for the whole chunk instead of the per-row attn_paged launches; the
  gated form (`gated`) keeps its path. Numerics: Q / K / V / P bf16 as Intel ships first; fp16 if the KL replay
  says so (the per-row form's experience). Gates: the card test, B-run (7K / 20K), `kld-gl.sh` replay against
  the exact path, then the decision on the default.

- **GLUE-ALL'S 20K COST, THE MECHANISM (code read, 15:5x):** every glued append waits on the DEVICE's previous append
  (glue_append: Z.prev_slot, l0.cpp ~1564) on the device's ONE in-order list Z.imm (compute group, l0.cpp ~1035).
  Under glue-all the compute stream's events are native slots; the stager's `rad_event_wait(transfer, free/gate)`
  (stager.cpp 163 / 182 / 236) then takes the native path (l0.cpp ~2999: wait + signal appended to Z.imm, the
  transfer stream npend) -> glue_on(transfer) -> copy_on glues the expert copies onto Z.imm too (l0.cpp ~1825). The
  prefill stager's copies (up to 3 layers ahead) are then in one total order with the compute kernels: no overlap,
  and they run on the compute engine instead of a copy engine. (Without glue-all those events are runtime events ->
  a runtime barrier, async, and the copies stay on the runtime queue.) Adapter options were tried (MD13-MD15): no fix.
  **THE TARGETED FORM (design, not built): per-stream glue order.** A second native immediate list a device for the
  mover's transfer stream (the copy group if the driver gives one in order, else a second compute list), marked
  by a role on L0Stream (a dispatch call from mover.cpp's stream creation, or the xp stream path); its glued appends
  wait on the STREAM's own previous slot (s.npend), not Z.prev_slot, and leave Z.prev_slot alone; cross-stream
  order only by explicit event waits (the ring is per device, so n_slot_event works across the two lists). Risk:
  anything relying on the device's total order (masked ordering bugs) -> gates: KL 24 stable documents, 7K
  logprobs, M-pair, and the 20K back to ~10.47.

- **WHY (reading, being proved): the default row grid has a latent bug the map does not.** The format C call gets
  off[0..n_reg]; the protected experts' rows follow the regular ones in the sort, past the call's live count, with
  REAL slots (sorted >= 0, not -1). In the row grid such a row binary-searches to the last regular expert; (i - first)
  % 64 can be 0, and rn = min(last - i, 64) with last < i wraps (unsigned) to 64 -> a 64-row block computed with the
  wrong expert's weights and written up to 63 rows PAST T (out of the output's rows: into whatever follows in the
  arena). The arch says the quantised down GEMM "zeroed their sorted rows as past its live count"
  (rad_block_moe_fp8.h:1799); the map does (tail entries from off[n_expert]); the row grid zeroes only sorted < 0
  rows. This also explains run 171's deterministic, unexplained 64-row vs 128-row difference (0.039: another block
  size, other wrong rows). The decode run kernel (kMT = 4) has the same wrap (up to 3 rows past T). THE TEST:
  RADIANCE_XE_I4I8_DPAS_SLMC=6 gives the row grid the map's rule (a row >= off[n_expert] is zeroed); config

- **A.4, the ESIMD probe -- the design (next run; not started this run for the budget):** a form "E1" of format C's down
  (<3,2,2,GL>) added to fc_tile_probe.cpp, timed and byte-compared by its harness against today's kernel through libxe.
  The exact arithmetic to keep (from t1_run_kernel): per column, lane 0 sums the even 64-K groups and lane 1 the odd ones
  in u order, each group's int32 dot (levels x int8 activations, order-free) then `acc += ((float)s * asc) * sbr`, and
  the column = lane 0's acc + lane 1's. What ESIMD changes, guided by A.2 / A.3: an ESIMD thread covers 16 columns as
  SIMD lanes (both lanes' sums kept separately, added at the end -- the same fp adds); one 2D block load fetches a
  group's codes for the 16 columns (16 rows x 32 bytes, pitch w_ld); the 16 int8 levels sit in a register and codes are
  decoded by register-indirect iselect (no SLM, a few ops a 16 codes); dp4a on the packed levels. Go at >= 25 % off the
  launch (66.4 -> <= 49.8 us), bit-identical.

  AND the 1-user text. -> NOT a race inside a step (the four lanes always agree) but the FIRST TIME A BATCH SHAPE RUNS: its
  passes are issued live while they are recorded, later ones replay the tape, and the 1-user phase only replays. The
  likeliest cause: a kernel whose live launch and taped replay give different bits** (a different form or argument on
  the live path). Next check (one card step, no drafting): the same with RADIANCE_L0_TAPE=0 (`-notape-`): both 4-user
  phases should then match each other.

  sequence, deterministically; the replay of a 4-sequence shape equals the 1-sequence text. So the run that records a
  >= 4-sequence shape takes a batch-dependent path its replay does not (the replay is batch-invariant here, the live
  issue is not).** The kernel is not identified yet: next, with tapes off, the forms one at a time (the expert run /

- **Note 199 item 3, the desk hypothesis (for the owner):** the faulting address is 0x00008000fffe0000 on both cards,
  three times. 0xFFFE0000 = (uint32)(-1) << 17: a block id of -1 times a 2^17-byte (128 KiB) unit computed in 32 bits,
  added to a pool base -- an unallocated block-table entry used as an index, not a stale data pointer. The one reader
  known to go past what it owns is the MTP head's first draft (it attends 1 + n_spec slots past its position; upstream
  64c652f, our RADIANCE_MTP_HIST_CTX): when that over-read crosses into a block the sequence does not hold yet, the
  table entry there is -1. With more sequences drafting, more rows sit at a block edge each step; after the warm-up the
  loan to the expert slab leaves fewer free blocks, so a row's lookahead lands on the edge more often. Ranked: (1) the
  over-read reaching an unallocated block (fits the address, the 6-user dependence, and the warm-up's other symptom,
  the stale K / V the over-read found); (2) the loan's recall leaving a weight-table entry naming a moved unit (fits
  "the weight table could not be patched", but a moved unit's old address is still mapped -- wrong data, not a page
  fault). **The one card test: the C30 phase (6 drafting users, warm-up on, image 248) with RADIANCE_MTP_HIST_CTX=1 --
  clean confirms (1) (the over-read bounded to the sequence's own length); if it still faults, the same phase with
  RADIANCE_KV_LEND=0 tests (2).** Not run: note 199 forbids 6-user drafting on the cards until the owner says so.
  **UPDATE after C31 / C32 -- hypothesis (0), now the likeliest: VRAM exhaustion.** C31 aborted with the same
  OUT_OF_RESOURCES at 5 users with drafting OFF and the driver at 38-51 MiB free; C32 with 4 GiB headroom ran clean. All
  four aborts were in the 6-seat form at 2 GiB headroom with the most recorded pass shapes (the warm-up's, or drafting's
  at 2-3 users); the page fault is consistent with a kernel reading a buffer whose allocation failed (a base plus
  (uint32)(-1) << 17 is what an index of -1 into such a buffer gives). The cheaper confirming card test is then C30's
  phase with `-hr4g-` -- but it drafts at 6 users, so it waits for the owner.

  - **NOTE 224 ITEM 3's OPEN HALF, ANSWERED FROM THE CODE AND THE RECORD (desk, 10:5x-11:0x; no card step): the 221 us
    step boundary is NOT host work.** engine.cpp's step loop issues the NEXT step's forward pass BEFORE this step's
    readback (`issue_ahead`, l.388 / l.779: `pipelining_ = step_ahead && !kld && !embedding && (serial_drafting() ||
    block_drafting() || n_spec <= 0)`; RADIANCE_STEP_AHEAD=0 turns it off and is set only by the `-nopipe-` / `bestrnp`
    configs of run 162, not by any service or M-step config), so at the single prompt the host's accept / commit / plan /
    build / pre (~0.03-0.05 ms a step by the phase line: plan 0.01, pre 0.02, build / commit / draft 0.00) and the ranks'
    enqueue (3.67 ms a step at steady state, H157's last step lines) all run while the card executes the next pass; the
    run-162 `-nopipe-` rotation (-3.8 %) measured what the boundary costs when the host IS on the path. What the tape
    timeline charges as "logits_i8_rows @T22 -> qk_rope_table @T24, 221 us" is therefore a DEVICE-SIDE gap between the
    verify tape's last kernel and the issued-ahead tape's first kernel: in that interval sit the step-end event record
    (mark_step_end), the readback of the sampled rows (collect_issue; a host-pinned target) and the next play's ring-slot
    handshake -- none of them kernel spans, so the edge shows no "(copy)" between the two kernels. The nap cap's null
    result (run 272, M375-M377) is consistent: the wake-up latency is off the critical path. => No host part >= 50 us
    is removable (the owner's design condition is not met on the host side); the remaining question is device / driver
    side (whether the readback is a blit on the compute list or a copy-engine hand-off, and the ring-slot event wait at
    the play boundary). A diagnostic that would split the 221 us: the tape profiler recording the event-record and
    copy commands as spans at the step boundary (RADIANCE_L0_NTAPE_EDGES's edge list already carries copies elsewhere)
    -- ~$20, one build + one profiled M-step; worth at most 0.8 % of the step. Recorded in WAITING as a proposal, not
    started (the coordinator's call; the cards are better spent on the A / B default flip when the owner answers).**

- **The expert prefill algorithm -- the design brief for run 175 (written 07:35, nothing built).** The item:
  the expert DPAS kernel (scoreboard row 1) is ~2.3 s of a 4,096-row chunk's ~3.3 s device time, at ~1.5 % of
  the matrix units' peak; run 170's ablations and run 171's five exact restructurings showed its 64-row
  form is at this structure's floor: the per-64-K-group chain (the 4-bit decode, the shared-memory staging
  of B, two barriers, the MMAs, the per-group scaling) under lockstep threads, re-run by every 64-row block
  of an expert's run (~3.4 blocks an expert for the 7K). The algorithm: (1) a decode pass once a layer --
  one kernel over the layer's routed experts' codes (the staging ring's pooled experts plus the resident
  ones) writing int8 B tiles in the DPAS packed layout ([tile][step] 32 k x 16 n, the trunk's gemm_i8a8
  layout) into a VRAM scratch; (2) the GEMM reading those tiles straight from global memory with
  joint_matrix_load (the trunk's kernel does this through a shared-memory stage; here the B tile is
  loaded per sub-group from global -- L2-resident across the ~3.4 blocks that share it), the A tile
  staged as today, the per-64-K-group int32 sums scaled exactly as today (the same (sum x asc) x sbr order
  -> the bits byte-equal to B111's form, the gate). Memory: a rank's decoded int8 experts for one layer =
  the codes x 2 = ~2 x 168-207 MiB of pooled ones + the resident ones' share -> a ~0.5 GB scratch a rank,
  double-buffered to overlap the next layer's decode = ~1 GB of VRAM taken from the expert slab (the slab is
  ~28 GB: ~3.5 % fewer resident experts for decode's heat). Expected: the GEMM loses the decode (0.59 s of
  the 7K), the B staging (0.56) and most of the chain's barriers and shared-memory traffic -- the ablation
  table's named parts, ~1.5 s of the kernel's 3.3 s a 7K -- and gains L2 reads of B; the decode pass costs
  ~0.1 s a 7K (0.7 GB a layer at 600 GB/s x 48, overlapped). A 4,096-row chunk from ~3.3 to ~2.0 s; the 7K
  cold 7.0 -> ~5.5, warm 5.8 -> ~4.4. **CORRECTED 07:40 (the numbers above were too optimistic):** the
  mover's units say a rank holds 2.4 MB of codes an expert (1.45 MiB gate_up + 992 KiB down) and ~85 % of
  the experts resident (the stager stages only ~85 MB a layer a rank = ~35 experts); a 4,096-row chunk
  routes to every expert, so a layer's decoded int8 B is 256 x 4.8 MB = ~1.2 GB A RANK, and a double buffer
  2.4 GB (8 % of the slab) -- not 0.5 GB; and the decode pass writes 1.2 GB and the GEMM reads it back:
  2.4 GB of VRAM traffic a layer a projection, ~0.4 s a chunk at 600 GB/s, against the ablation table's
  decode 0.43 + staging 0.40 s a chunk that it removes. NET ~0.4 s a chunk (~−0.55 s on the 7K, −8 %) for
  two runs' work and 8 % of the expert slab: NOT the lever it looked; parked. What would make it pay: a
  persistent-kernel form (one work-group an expert, looping over its row blocks with B decoded once into
  shared memory per K group) -- which needs the K loop outermost and the row blocks' accumulators to live
  somewhere (registers cannot hold 3-4 blocks: the RT = 16 form was slower under grf 256), so an exact
  two-pass split-K (fp32 partials in VRAM, 4 KB a row x 24 groups) -- a design for a later run, after the
  owner's four calls, which together reach the 5 s target on their own (5.8 warm now, the cold second is
  the warm-up). The build order: (a) the decode kernel + the int8 GEMM kernel in libxe
  behind RADIANCE_XE_I4I8_DECODE_ONCE=1, with a CPU-device check of the decode kernel (the int8 GEMM cannot
  run on the CPU device: the int8 joint_matrix is refused there, as fcdpas showed) and the card's byte-equal
  gate; (b) the scratch: the op's declared scratch (the attention op's `xe_rad_attn_qsa_fmha_scratch` pattern
  -- the registry row's scratch hook sized from the geometry) is the engine-sanctioned way, no new
  allocation path; (c) the decode pass issued by the op itself at a layer's first call (the op sees the
  layer's expert table; a per-layer "decoded" flag in the scratch's header keyed on the staging's
  publication epoch -- the staged pointers change every chunk) -- so the engine's scheduler, stager and
  tables stay untouched. Two runs of work (~$120); the owner's memory call is in WAITING, and by UNATTENDED's
  rule the decision is: build it behind the flag (reversible, the slab's loss measurable by the M-pair).**

staging's 1.15, the A loads inside the 1.3 s remainder) are load latencies on the chain, which the prefetch

- **The "shape" refusal, from the code (23:25-23:55, no card):** the text is RAD_E_SHAPE's (rad_types.h:60). The op's
  RAD_E_SHAPE exits: head_dim / gqa; kv rank 4 / sel rank 2; kv cache shape; sel rows / inner stride; seqused rows /
  contiguity; sel entries / table width; the context check; the FMHA's can_implement. The operands as the engine
  builds them (issue.cpp: RAD_OPK_BUF = the declared shape with dim 0 narrowed to rows; RAD_OPK_RAW: praw2 -> rank 2
  [1][pitch] strides [pitch][1], praw -> rank 1 [1]; RAD_OPK_KV = the group's rank-4 cache): q = brows(w.q, T),
  kv_cache(kv, layer), out = brows(w.attn.x, T) are the dense path's own operands to attn_paged, which checks them
  the same way (xe_attn.cpp:273-283) -> pass; sel / seqused are the brow_slices the per-row sparse path hands
  attn_paged in its bt / su slots (rank 2, shape[0] == rows, stride[1] == 1; contiguous) -> pass; bt = praw2(table,
  I32, 1, pitch) -> rank 2, max_blocks = pitch > 0 (kvb is non-null: `fmha` requires table && used); cx = praw(used,
  I32, 1) -> rank 1 I32; can_implement is `true` by construction (the mainloop copy's line 308, the epilogue's 144).
  **So the only RAD_E_SHAPE these operands can reach is the context check (`ctx <= 0 || ctx < T || ctx >
  max_blocks * bs`), whose value is the device read: ctx_kernel -> the op's USM host word -> the host.** Two ways the
  read gives a refusing value, both in the code: (a) glue mode (l0.cpp n_hook_device, the default since run 126):
  while a stream's last work is a native tape play, a libxe launch is appended to the device's immediate list, not
  the SYCL queue, so the op's `qq->wait()` covers nothing and the sentinel -1 is read ("ctx <= 0") -- but B100's
  refusal was at the process's step 0, before any play, so the glue was off there and the wait was real; hence (b):
  **the ctx_kernel itself faulted (the CAT error at 22:58:48, ~3 s after the request came in), the job was killed,
  the wait returned, the host word still -1 -> "shape", both ranks alike.** Which memory: the kernel touches two
  words, `used` (the batch's device copy, the engine's allocation, made resident at allocation under
  RADIANCE_L0_EXPLICIT_RESIDENCY=1 + DisableIndirectAccess=1, l0.cpp:285-324) and the op's own USM host word
  (sycl::malloc_host on the rank's queue -- the only memory in that launch the engine did not allocate; the engine's
  residency rule covers its own allocations and skips RAD_MEM_HOST; m3 fault 35 is the precedent: a libxe allocation
  a kernel reached without residency -> the same "CAT error, class=ccs, Fault response -EIO, Timedout job"
  signature). **Most likely: the ctx_kernel's store into the op's host word.** The alternative -- `used` itself not
  device-readable at a sparse chunk (no kernel of the sparse path reads it: attn_paged's dense path reads `used`
  only below 2,051 tokens; the per-row path gets qsa_sequ instead) -- cannot be excluded from the code alone; the
  rework reads neither, so the one allowed step tests the rest.

  declared scratch (the engine's arena, resident; a scratch hook sized from the declared params: inv [2 x max_ctx /
  bs] i32, bits [T_pad x nw_max] u32 with nw_max = ceil(max_ctx / bs / 32), kd / vd [kvh][max_ctx][256] bf16, a few
  device words: ~72 MiB at this geometry; RAD_E_SCRATCH at issue if short); (2) no host read -- the context length
  taken ON THE DEVICE from qsa_sequ[T-1] (the last row's seqused, an arena buffer the per-row path already reads),
  clamped to [T, max_ctx] into a scratch word by a one-item kernel; the prep kernels launched at the host-known
  maxima (the table width, max_ctx) and bounded by the word; the FMHA reading seq_len_kv from a device pointer (a
  copy of xe_fmha_fwd_kernel.hpp under fmha/, shadowed like the mainloop; the non-varlen layout kept -- the varlen
  form packs its strides from the shape, a different layout); (3) every launch through the engine's launch path so

sentinel (the other rank's host word) and "shape", and the CAT errors (a kernel reaching the other card's
memory). Fix: one buffer set per queue (a mutex-guarded table); a rank's own calls are serial. Rebuilding libxe

  native Level Zero lists on a device that has them (xe_lanes.h launch_as: `if (rad_l0k_rec_device(&q) >= 0)
  launch_native(...)`), so (a) the op's `qq->wait()` on the SYCL queue after its ctx_kernel waits for nothing
  that matters: the host word keeps my −1 sentinel -> "ctx <= 0" -> RAD_E_SHAPE on every run since B98 (B97
  tried a queue memcpy from the same word: "invalid argument"); (b) the FMHA goes through compat's own
  submission on the SYCL queue, unordered against the engine's kernels and the op's prep kernels; (c) the prep
  kernels, if they ran unordered before the selection / cache store of the chunk, read page ids that are not
  there yet -> the bitmap kernel's atomicOr past its buffer -> the CCS CAT error (the same signature all three
  times). The shared-buffer race (fixed) was real but secondary. **Fix design for the next permitted run:**
  (1) no host wait: the FMHA in its varlen form (device cumulative lengths: cu_q = [0, T] written by a kernel,
  cu_k = [0, ctx] with ctx copied on the device from the `used` word), the prep kernels bounded by the device
  word and launched by the maximum (max_blocks x bs); (2) the FMHA launched through XE_LAUNCH like every libxe
  kernel: a wrapper kernel around cutlass::device_kernel<FMHAKernel> with the launch path's dynamic LDS for its
  SharedStorage (check launch_as's lds mechanism against compat's work_group_scratch_size); (3) the buffers
  grown only between steps (never inside a step's launch sequence). Then the 7K alone, the klog, the replay.

- **So today's all-reduce's 25 us a launch is its store pattern, not the link:** the engine runs the LL form
  (ar_kernel<0, false, 4>: each payload word with the sequence number in one uncached 8-byte store, the reader polls
  each word), 4,096 words a launch at 4 rows -- one PCIe write a word. The handshake is ~4.5 us; the message's bytes
  at the link's rate ~1.5 us. A wide-store LL (a lane storing 16 / 32 / 64 bytes of tagged words at once; the tags
  still checked a word, so a store landing in pieces is still read right) could bring a launch from ~25 us towards
  ~6-8: ~1.8 ms a step (~5 %) -- above the rotation gate, if the stores really coalesce under the uncached hint or

- **Note 165 item 1, the reading (14:50-15:00) and the design for the next run.** The serial drafter
  (engine_draft.cpp): the host issues the whole step (the verify, the history pass, rounds 2..3) without waiting
  and reads the StepSlots back once; `finish_serial_drafter` then publishes the rounds' tokens through
  `sched_.set_draft(seq, tokens, done)` -- the next verify's rows = the published drafts + 1. **The gate lives
  there: publish 2 of the 3 drafts when the third round's confidence is under the threshold** (draft.h's own
  caveat -- "the scheduler picks the depth before the drafter runs" -- does not bind here: the depth of the NEXT
  verify is chosen after this step's rounds are read back, which already happens; no extra host wait, and the
  3-row verify is a second recorded shape, as the owner says). What is missing is the confidence: the draft rows'
  token comes from `argmax_kernel` (libxe/ports/r4d_sample_stages_f32.cpp:351, launched by r4d_sample_argmax_f32
  ~1160; the greedy path never runs the softmax chain), so the cheapest confidence is the top-2 logit margin from
  the same walk (each thread keeps best and second; the wave reduction merges pairs), written as a float a row
  beside the token -- a new libxe entry (`sample_argmax_margin_f32`, a null margin pointer = today's kernel) so
  the ABI and the AMD copy stay; the advance that copies S.tok[round] (sched/advance_impl.h:174 / 182 / 199,
  ADV_ROUND / ADV_TAKE) copies the margin into a new `float conf[1 + RAD_SCHED_MAX_SPEC]` of StepSlot (advance.h;
  a shared layout both backends compile). Then: `RADIANCE_DRAFT_GATE=<margin>`; stats every 2048 verifies as
  NGRAM_STATS does (steps published at depth 2 / 3, tokens a step, the margin's histogram); three thresholds at
  most on two M-steps (the story prompt and CE2, texts must stay M229's / M236's); the best one's rotation against
  H114 at >= +1.5 % median. **Estimate:** the fourth row costs 4.9 ms a step (1a) and the third draft is accepted in
  ~35-40 % of the rotation's steps, so a perfect gate is worth ~3 ms a step (~8 %) at no token; a real one perhaps
  half -- above the gate if the margin predicts acceptance as it does for EAGLE-style heads. Product-of-three
  gating (the note's p1 x p2 x p3) is the same plumbing with three margins; start with the third round's alone.
  Not started: a 2-3 h build (kernel + ABI + slots + gate + stats + image), better begun fresh.

  (xe_moe_i4i8.cpp moe_i4i8_run_kernel), not the router -- the GEMM work-group holds the expert's table entry
  (pointer) and each row's rank (sorted slot % top_k): an entry off the device (the pinned pool: on this platform
  device and host USM lie on opposite sides of 2^47, probed at init, refused otherwise) at rank >= R drops the row
  (zeros out, so the gather adds nothing) and a run dropped whole skips the weight reads. **No renormalisation**:
  with expert parallelism each rank sees only its own experts' residency, so a per-rank renormalisation would make
  the two ranks' partial sums inconsistent (the "why not"); the heat engine still sees the demand (the routing and
  sort are untouched), so a cold expert can still warm up. Stats in device memory (pairs by rank live / off-device /
  dropped, runs skipped whole), read once a step through xe_ar2_stalls, printed every 200 calls. The row's new init

    nothing;

      in the same order (fb0 = 1, fb = 2, fb2 = 3), so a caller naming one slot in every column ends with the
      same bytes.

    (128 / VS x 8 >= 256, so VS <= 4), and at VS 8 two slices would share a 32-row group's factors (a write /
    replay race in the anchor form). It would need the convolution's staging reworked (two channels a thread).

      (~0.4 ms a step at ~3 us each).

      matrix form does.

    - The state stays in accumulators (2 x BV/16 tiles a sub-group), decayed by joint_matrix_apply.
    - The emulated form's roundings are kept: W, sA, V', the S copy and gs*K round half-away through f2bf. Rows past
      the chunk's end stage zeros.

## Design (run 1, 08:30 UTC)
- Facts checked: intel/llvm v7.2.0 names unnamed-lambda kernels through `__builtin_sycl_unique_stable_name`
  (`kernel_desc.hpp`), so `sycl::get_kernel_id<decltype(lambda)>()` finds a `launch_as` kernel without naming
  it; the loader is 1.29 / headers 1.16 (`zeCommandListImmediateAppendCommandListsExp`, `ZE_COMMAND_LIST_FLAG_IN_ORDER`);
  the dynamic work-group scratch is a kernel parameter (`kind_dynamic_work_group_memory`), so a `launch_as`
  kernel has two arguments: the tuple and the local-memory size; N1 (m2 run 14) showed the SYCL in-order queue's
  native handle is an immediate command list and a native launch of the tuple kernel is identical.
- Channel: `abi/rad_l0_rec.h` (the recorder ABI) -- `rad_l0k_rec_device(queue)` (-1 unless this thread records
  natively on that stream), `rad_l0k_rec_launch(queue, sycl::kernel*, grid, block, arg0, size, lds)`,
  `rad_l0k_rec_copy2d`; function table installed by l0.cpp into librad_l0k (`rad_l0k_set_rec`). libxe's
  `launch_as`/`launch_as_grf256` and the core's three kernels (advance, fill, wtab patch) ask it first; the
  backend's memcpy/memset/2D/ranges/list copies append natively.
- Backend: a native tape = one `ZE_COMMAND_LIST_FLAG_IN_ORDER` regular list per segment (closed at tape_mark,
  executed at once by appending it to the stream's immediate list with a wait on the queue's last event and a
  signal event from a per-device ring; the signal event is imported as a sycl::event and a barrier on the queue
  keeps the SYCL runtime's own order). The recorder owns its kernel objects (`zeKernelCreate` on the bundle's
  module, by name), so the runtime's kernel argument state is never raced. A play appends the stretch's lists in
  one call. Event records inside a tape need no device command (one in-order list); waits on outside events are
  refused as before. A segment whose stream's last event moved outside the recorder (a direct SYCL submission)
  refuses the tape. Deferred free as before (`t.last` = the barrier event). The SYCL-graph tapes stay for the
  CPU device and `RADIANCE_L0_TAPE=graph`.
- Not in this item: merged one-list-per-stretch from kept descriptors (the hybrid cache's shape), after the
  per-list cost is measured; the MTP by-value argument (item 2).

  **Question for the report's prompt-10 paragraph (run 41): what `--kv-cache-dtype` does production (1.11.0-keyenv)
  run?** The port's args carry fp8 (since milestone 1). On prompt 10 the card gives 'The' -0.473 with fp8 K/V and
  -0.0045 with bf16 K/V; production says -0.050 (note 40). If production runs bf16, the port's fp8 K/V path (libxe's
  FP8 conversions, or fp8 K/V itself) is the whole divergence and the comparison is not like-for-like; if production
  runs fp8 too, the port's fp8 K/V path differs from production's by ~0.4 nats on this prompt. The production config

## Note 53: the host expert path, sized (run 65)
The three measurements, as far as the heat rules allowed:
1. **Host memory bandwidth** (N53, 1 thread, rad-avx-bench `--peak`): DRAM read **29.5 GB/s**, triad 25.0 (AMD Ryzen 9
   5950X, AVX2, no AVX-512). The 2-thread figure was not reached: one core at full boost took Tctl to 75-79 C in 4-9 s
   (N53, N53b), so CPU-bound benches wait for the heatsink (decision, run 65).
2. **The CPU time of one missed unit**: not measured (the same heat stop, inside the bench's setup). Its bandwidth
   floor from (1): a 1.24 MiB unit at 29.5 GB/s is **~44 us a thread** (note 53 assumed ~30 us); the codebook decode's
   compute on AVX2 is unmeasured, so the projection below brackets it at 1x and 2x the floor.
3. **The misses' distribution** (H19 on :62, f593efb's counters): 81 misses a pass over 49 routed layers, **1.0-2.5 a
   layer (median 1.7), spread evenly**; dispatches by their misses 0: 42.6 %, 1: 27.8 %, 2: 14.6 %, 3-4: 10.3 %,
   5-8: 3.3 %, 9-16: 0.7 %, 17+: 0.8 %. **A layer's misses arrive together (one dispatch), so one hand-off a layer
   suffices; a pass hands off on ~28 of 49 layers, mostly one or two units.**

**Projected exposed miss time a pass** (per hand-off layer: 25 us of card-host signalling + ceil(misses / threads) x
the unit time, less the ~50 us the card spends on the layer's resident experts in parallel; summed over the histogram):

| cores (host threads) | unit at the floor (44 us) | unit at 2x the floor |
|---|---:|---:|
| today (misses read over PCIe, the brief's fit 150-220 us each) | 10.4-15.3 ms | |
| 2 (1) | 2.5 ms | 5.7 ms |
| 4 (2) | 1.2 ms | 3.2 ms |
| 8 (6) | 0.7 ms | 2.1 ms |

On H19's ~95-100 ms rotation step (MTP on) that is **-8 to -14 ms at 8 cores: +9 to +17 %, ~35.5 -> 39-42 tok/s**,
the low end of note 53's +15-25 %; nothing on the single prompt. Sized in runs: the host-wait prototype on the tiny
model (1-2 runs; it decides feasibility: two events a layer inside a recorded pass), the skip in moe_planes_v2m and the
host row path with the CPU / oracle gates (2 runs), the 11-request agreement with the flag on (1 window), the speed A/B
after Nov 1 (1 window). Design: `m3/design-host-experts.md`.

## Note 50: the four leads (run 60)
1. **Prefill chunk (item 1).** B12 = the control at 4,096 with the service numerics (the matrix expert form on,
   gemm_nt bf16): **7K 27.34 s (205 tok/s), 20K 48.73 s** (the GEMV form's B11: 32.62 / 58.77). B13 =
   `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` alone: **the chunk stayed 4,096** -- plan_chunk splits at the linear-state
   checkpoint interval first (sched/geometry.cpp:154-166: the chunk is min(checkpoint_interval x prefill_span,
   max_tok), and the log line says "(the checkpoint interval, not the budget)"), so the flag only grew the arena
   (1.20 -> 2.02 GiB a card plus 2 x 175 MiB scratch; the two pools 53.67 -> 51.67 GiB) and raised the prefill
   stager's threshold from "a step of more than 1,024 tokens" to "more than 4,096" (engine_bringup.cpp:3464-3488:
   the threshold is the largest arena level below the span's), so the 4,096-token chunks lost the staged-experts
   path: **32.20 / 51.92 s (+18 % / +7 %)**, a worse configuration, not a chunk measurement. The A/B proper:
   `--prefill-span 2` with the budget 8,192 (chunks of two intervals, the checkpoint grid still 4,096: B14) and
   `--prefill-span 4` at 16,384 (B15, if the arena allows: B12 / B13 peaked at 31.5 GB a card of 32), staged on
   intel-host (m3/B14, m3/B15; configs nomtpmx8ks / nomtpmx16ks in m3-prefill.sh). Strata's own measurement of the
   knob (docs/INTEL.md): 8,192 beats 4,096 by 10-11 % at 16K and 15-16 % at 32K prompts on the B70 (IQ3_S), the
   first token not bit-identical (KL 1.1e-2 at 16K, the same top-1); their default is 4,096, with 8,192
   recommended on >= 24 GB Battlemage above a 32K context. **The service keeps 4,096 until B14 / B15 say
   otherwise** (B13's form is slower and takes 1 GiB a card from the experts).
   **Run 61's answers**: B14 (the span form) changed nothing (27.83 / 49.06 s) because the scheduler takes a span
   only for a lone prompt of eight intervals or more -- 32,768 tokens (engine.cpp:1613-1620; serve.log:162) -- so
   RADIANCE_PREFILL_SPAN_MIN (b3bd92e, :59) makes the minimum settable for the A/B; B15 (the interval form:
   `--checkpoint-interval 8192`) gave **the 7K prompt in one 5,604-token chunk 25.92 s (-5 %)** and the 20K prompt
   **70.14 s with cache 0** (the coarser checkpoint grid dropped the 5,568-token prefix hit; 231 tok/s on all 16,184
   tokens against B12's 218 on its 10,616 new ones: **+6 % a token from the larger chunk**). B16 next window: the
   span form at the minimum 4,096 (8,192-token chunks, the 4,096 grid kept); B17 at 16,384 if the arena allows.
2. **Heat decay and move budget (item 2).** How prefill chunks credit the heat, read before changing anything
   (heat.cpp:217-222, heat.h:71-77): observe() runs once a layer a step; when a histogram's selections exceed
   credit_cap = 512 the whole histogram is scaled to 512 selections, order preserved -- a 4,096-token chunk
   credits like 64 decode tokens at top-8, which is the rescale the vLLM RFC the owner cites arrived at (heat.h
   records upstream's mixed-workload replay: decode hit rate 77.3 % uncapped, 78.9 % at 1,024, 79.0 % at 512 or
   256). The rotation's prompts are 6-462 tokens, so the cap binds only on the three tool prompts (348-462 tokens
   x 8 = 2,784-3,696 selections -> 512); prefill credit is not what churns the rotation, and no rescale is
   needed. Decay: heat.h:41-43 records upstream's replay at 64 swaps a step -- hit rate flat from 0.8 to 0.95 and
   falling above it (77.1 % at 0.98, 74.2 % at 0.99: "a longer memory ranks experts the conversation has moved
   past above the current ones") -- the prior against the two values; measured on the rotation anyway, as asked.
   **The knobs are written** (engine_bringup.cpp: RADIANCE_PLACE_DECAY in [0.5, 1), RADIANCE_PLACE_MOVES in
   [1, 64] -- lower only, the shadow and turnover slots are sized from RAD_PLACE_MOVES_PER_STEP at plan time;
   m3/commit-heat-knobs.txt), uncommitted until a build; the configs mtp4gmx (the control at the service
   setting), mtp4gd98, mtp4gd99, mtp4gm32, mtp4gm16 are in m2-heat.sh. Five 5-minute rotations = two windows
   (H15-H19), each read with m3/stats_delta.py (misses a step, readmits) and m3/heat_median.py.
3. **Strata (item 3)**: docs/INTEL_ARC.md, docs/INTEL.md and PR #423 read (MIT; the SYCL port is a SYCLomatic
   translation of their CUDA engine, 32-lane sub-groups "written for warps"; docs/INTEL_PERFORMANCE.md is 404).
   Taken for the report, cited: (a) **GDN: Strata has no chunk scan** -- a sub-group recurrence kernel
   (STRATA_GDN_XE) that is OFF on Battlemage because it cost 3.5 % (1,251 -> 1,207 tok/s at 4,095 tokens);
   DeltaNet is 5.8 % of a 40K prompt there; XMX is not used for it -- no shape to borrow for our 23 %; (b)
   **prompt attention on XMX (STRATA_PROMPT_ATTN_XMX=1) is 24-27 % slower on the B70** than their per-cell
   kernel, and their joint_matrix GEMM is opt-in because it loses too -- the matrix unit is not a sure gain for
   attention on this card (ours is 7 % of the first token); (c) the **int8 prefill expert path**: ESIMD kernels
   decode the quantized experts in registers and multiply q8_1 activations on the s8 DPAS unit, on by default on
   Battlemage: +21 % at 1,024 tokens, +12 % at 4,095 (B70, IQ3_S), KL 2e-4 nat, top-1 99.7 %; it stops winning
   above ~130 rows an expert (chunks >= 8,192) -- the analogue of our matrix expert form (fp8 E4M3 experts on
   DPAS, exact), already the default; (d) their prompt rate **980-1,002 tok/s at 4,095 tokens on one B70** (IQ3_S,
   3-bit experts, 11.5k of 24.6k resident) against our 205 tok/s at 5,604 tokens on two cards (fp8 experts, TP2):
   the 5x is the prefill gap, of which the GDN scan (23 %) and hc_read_a (15 %) are the named pieces; their
   decode 30.5 (prose) to 40.8 (code) tok/s with MTP at 66-90 % accepted, against our 42 alone (45 %) and the
   rotation's 30.5 (69 %); (e) their expert reads for prompts: a 12-thread stager (STRATA_STAGER_THREADS) and a
   256-token first chunk so the card starts early (STRATA_PREFILL_FIRST).
4. **Stage D facts (item 4)**: the VRAM floor stays (Strata's rule is the same: on the xe driver an allocation
   past VRAM does not fail, the driver evicts into host RAM and can livelock the machine; they leave ~1.5 GB free
   and reserve 1,024 MiB up to a 32K context, 2,048 above -- ours is the 4 GiB headroom plus the 1 GiB floor).
   JIT: libxe is AOT for bmg-g31 (libxe/CMakeLists.txt:7) and the SYCL cache is persistent on intel-host's volume, so
   a start compiles nothing of ours; **the load's 87 s is the container read: 64.4 GiB in 80.6 s at 0.9 GB/s,
   74.4 s of it the disk** (B12 serve.log:111) -- the stage D image carries AOT kernels already, and Strata's
   47-s first start is their JIT build's (their AOT build compiles nothing at first start; their load to first
   token is 26 s after a pipelined fill, ours 87 s at the disk's rate). Strata runs SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT=0 after
   a crash of the persistent cache on Xe2 at the first compile; ours has run =1 on the shared volume through ~150
   starts without one (recorded as a platform note). The v1 adapter (UR_LOADER_USE_LEVEL_ZERO_V2=0) is what every
   step and the unit run; xe job_timeout_ms untouched; Resizable BAR on.

`m3/service/` on amd-host, mirrored at `/mnt/fast-storage/models/test/radiance-intel/m3/service/` on intel-host: the Quadlet

`RADIANCE_XE_LAUNCH_PROFILE=1` with `RADIANCE_L0_QUEUE_PROFILING=1` (e7ea49f): every live launch's device time from
the queue's event stamps. 5,604 tokens in three chunks (2,048 / 2,048 / 1,508); 427,356 launches timed over both
ranks, 65.1 s of device time in all = ~32.5 s a rank against a 36.9 s first token (35.9-36.4 unprofiled): the first
token is the device time. Per rank, by share:

| share | s a rank | launches a rank | us a launch | kernel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 22.9 % | 7.5 | 108 | 69,140 | `r4d_gdn_chunk_scan_kernel` (libr4d's HIP port, 36 GDN layers x 3 chunks) |
| 16.2 % | 5.3 | 192 | 27,440 | `moe_planes_v2m_kernel<1,4>` (the expert GEMV, the down projection) |

| 15.4 % | 5.0 | 388 | 12,955 | `hc_read_a_kernel` (the HyperConnection read at M rows) |
| 12.1 % | 3.9 | 204,546 | 19.2 | `gemv_bf16_kernel<...,4>` (`gemm_nt` bf16: one launch a token a layer) |
| 7.2 % | 2.4 | 288 | 8,178 | `attn_split_kernel<8,...>` (the paged attention, per query row) |

| 1.9 % | 0.6 | 388 | 1,593 | `ar_kernel` (the all-reduce) |

| 1.9 % | 0.6 | | | everything else (58 kernels) |

What it says: the two expert GEMVs are a third of the first token (the matrix form B3, off by default, halves them:
B3f 31.0 s), the GDN chunk scan a quarter (one HIP port, 69 ms a launch: the next port), the HyperConnection read a
sixth (per-row at M rows), and the bf16 `gemm_nt` is launched once a token (204,546 launches at the 19-us floor: a
batched form at M rows is ~0.1 s), attention 7 %. The trunk GEMM is done (1.4 %); the all-reduce is 2 %.

## Note 48: the n-gram lookups' skew (the hot-tier curve)
Method: `RADIANCE_NGRAM_TRACE=<file>` (c5e4c8c, image :49) makes the gather that serves the n-gram table
(libref's embed_gather on intel-host) append one record a call: six int64 (-1, M, row_bytes, rank, vocab_offset, n_vocab)
then the M global row ids; `python3 -I m3/ngram_tiers.py <file>` maps each row read to its 4 KiB page(s) of the
51.2 GB table (320,001,536 rows x 160 bytes; both ranks hold the whole table, so rank 0's records are counted once)
and prints the share of the page touches a hot tier would serve: frequency-ranked (an oracle over the run: the tier
holds the run's most-touched pages) and LRU (a cache that learns as it goes, over the trace's order; its misses
include every first touch).

**Decode: the 11-prompt rotation, H11t (run 51; 29 requests, ~4 minutes, MTP on):** 1,674 gathers, 167,440 rows read
(100 a gather on average: ~50 n-gram rows a decode step over the batch's tokens), 172,995 page touches, **38,123
distinct pages = 0.16 GB = 0.30 % of the table**, 4.5 touches a page.

| hot tier | frequency-ranked hit | LRU hit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 GB | 100 % | 78 % |
| 2 GB | 100 % | 78 % |
| 4 GB | 100 % | 78 % |
| 8 GB | 100 % | 78 % |
| 16 GB | 100 % | 78 % |

By frequency the tier that serves 50 / 80 / 90 / 95 % of the touches is 0.03 / 0.09 / 0.12 / 0.14 GB; the LRU figure is
flat at 78 % because the remaining 22 % are the compulsory first touches (38,123 of 172,995) -- the rotation never
re-touches enough to evict anything from even 1 GB. **The owner's rule (8 GB or less at >= 80 % of decode lookups) is
met by two orders of magnitude on this sample, with the caveat that the sample is 11 prompts cycling for 4 minutes:
the distinct-page count grows with traffic diversity, and production's varied traffic is the real test (note 40).**
**Prefill: the 5,604-token prompt, B5t (run 52; MTP off):** 4 gathers (the chunks; 16 n-gram rows a token), 89,680
rows read, 93,062 page touches, **3,911 distinct pages = 0.02 GB = 0.03 % of the table**, 23.8 touches a page.

| hot tier | frequency-ranked hit | LRU hit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 GB (and every larger size) | 100 % | 95.8 % |

By frequency 50 / 80 / 90 / 95 % of the prefill's touches live on 368 / 593 / 668 / 895 pages (1.5 / 2.4 / 2.7 / 3.7 MB);
the LRU figure is flat at 95.8 % because 4.2 % are first touches. **What this says for the first token: the prompt's
n-gram reads touch 16 MB of the table, so the lookups' share of the 7K first token (m2: ~2 ms a token, ~11 s) is not
the table's placement; it is the host path (the host-site op's join of the device stream, and libref's element-wise
gather), to be sized with a profile before anything is built.** No tier is designed (note 48: the owner reads the
curve first); the decision rule's number is 0.09 GB for 80 % of decode touches on this sample.

## Production API
27 of 30 requests used (the helper's count, logs/prod-api.log): 15 in milestones 1-2, the 7K first token in run 49
(prod-7k), the 11 agreement requests with logprobs in run 60 (owner note 49; results-m3/prod/). 3 remain.

## Decisions
decision (run 68, the brief's #11): the bf16 decode GEMV is committed **opt-in** (98ae19b, RADIANCE_XE_MOE_BF16_GEMV=1; the default stays the WMMA form) and the service image stays :62 | alternative: default on (+7 % MTP off, +13 % MTP on, M34) | why: the rule written before the measurement was "commit if the 11 requests agree with production at least as often as AG1", and AG2 gave fully identical answers on 2 of 11 against 3 (one reasoning near-tie, 0.45 / 0.17 nat, moved; texts and tool calls unchanged). Note 49 shows the owner may well take the speed over a near-tie, but that choice is the owner's, not mine; the code, the switch and both measurements are in place, and the decision is put to the owner in STATE's blockers and the notification
decision (run 66): the protected-expert bf16 pair's decode GEMV (the brief's #11) goes before note 53's host-op prototype | alternative: the prototype first, as run 65's Next said | why: P6 measured the pair at 2.4 ms of the 28.9 ms 1-row step in its slow mode, a contained kernel with an existing pattern (the w4 GEMV beside it) and a gain measurable this week, while the split's speed cannot be measured before the heatsink (note 53) and its prototype needs the op, the plugin placement and the tape path at once
decision (run 65, owner note 53's measurements): no more CPU-bound bench attempts on intel-host before the heatsink; the per-unit CPU time is projected from N53's measured DRAM read rate and measured after Nov 1 | alternative: retry the bench with shorter iterations or a sleep between phases | why: one core at full boost took Tctl from 38-42 C to 75-79 C in 4-9 s twice (N53, N53b), before any timed call -- the bench's setup alone trips the guard, so shorter timing does not help, and note 53 forbids burst tests and CPU-ramp exceptions before the heatsink. The projection: a missed unit is 1.24 MiB, so at the measured 29.5 GB/s single-thread DRAM read it is ~44 us a thread if bandwidth-bound (note 53 assumed ~30 us at 40-45 GB/s); the codebook decode's compute is not measured, so ~44 us is a floor. The engine itself is unaffected: its threads mostly wait, and its rotations warm intel-host over minutes, not seconds
decision (run 64, owner notes 52-55, the order of work): (1) note 52 item 2's first piece (c1a9c94, the branch-free E4M3 decode) is done -- token-identical, the M-pair moved (MTP off -0.53 ms, MTP on +3.9 %) -- and :61 becomes the service image after a clean rotation on it; (2) note 53's three measurements next (N53: rad-avx-bench --peak / --moe at 1 and 2 threads, libavx's vectorised moe_gemm_q at the model's geometry with a new routing a call, rather than libref's element-by-element reference the note names, which would overstate the CPU cost several-fold; and the per-layer miss counters on a rotation), then the split behind a flag through the CPU / oracle / agreement gates; (3) the rest of note 52 item 2 (the hc kernels' structure: norm once a connection, all waves streaming, fused A+B) and note 54's three grid items after it; (4) the ~1.5 ms lost on the 1-row step since :36 is attributed with one profiled M-step (`profnomtp`) on :61 against P3, because every later decode A/B is read against that step | alternative: the hc structural rewrite first, as note 52's order alone says | why: note 53 (amended 13:55) puts its measurements "after item 2's card checks" and its split before the pool-mechanism measurement; the decode piece passed its card checks this window, the measurements are one cheap step and a counter that rides on the next rotation, and the split's correctness gates fit 2 CPUs while its speed A/B waits for the heatsink -- so it can be written in the days the speed tests cannot run
decision (run 63, owner note 52 item 1): item 1a (89bf7fb: under the floor, keep the tapes played in the last 2,048 passes) is the fix that lands now, and :60 becomes the service image; item 1b (composing a pass as a few large lists to bound the pool's VRAM) is not started this run and goes to the report's "what remains", sized | alternative: build 1b before measuring, as the note lists both | why: H17 measured the collapse gone with 1a alone -- requests 22+ at 35.7 tok/s against H11's 15.6, live passes 170 of 23,772 against 7,918 of 16,352, the brief's "achievable" figure for item 1 (35.75) reached; 1b's remaining value is the residency it would return (the pool's ~4.5 GB a card, the brief's #6: headroom 4 -> 2 GiB worth ~+1.75 tok/s measured in H5), which runs 42-45 could not get from the stretch cache's bound (H9) and which needs a tape-layer rewrite of l0.cpp's composed stretches; note 52's order puts the report draft next, and a same-image control (H18, the earlier rule via RADIANCE_TAPE_KEEP_PASSES=0) is the next window's first step so the report's before / after is like for like
decision (run 62, note 50 item 1 closed): **the service keeps 4,096-token chunks** (`--max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --checkpoint-interval 4096`, no span) | alternative: the interval form at 8,192 (B15: 7K -5 %, the 20K prefix hit lost) or the span form (B16: no change at 7K, -0.4 s at 20K, 1.6 GiB less expert residency) | why: on the prompts the targets name, the larger chunk saves one sweep of the pooled experts through the staging ring per merged chunk (~1.4 s at 7K) and nothing else; the span form cannot merge the 7K prompt's two chunks (a span starts from the second interval) and the interval form coarsens the checkpoint grid that the 20K prompt's 5,568-token prefix hit keys on (+21 s there); the residency the span plan's arena takes (B13 / B14: 1-2 GiB a card) is worth more to decode (the pool item) than 1.4 s of a 27-s first token; Strata's 10-16 % at 16K / 32K prompts is the regime past our targets. What would make the chunk pay: a per-chunk expert sweep that does not restart at every chunk (keep the ring's layer-ahead copies across a prompt's chunks), which is a stager change, sized in the report
decision (run 62, note 50 item 1): B17 (16,384-token chunks: the budget 16,384 with span 4) is not run; the window's remaining minutes go to H16 (the heat A/B on :59) | alternative: run B17 as the note's "if the arena allows" item | why: the arena allows it (B16's span plan took 2.0 GiB a card at a 31.5 GB peak), but a span starts from a prompt's second interval, so at these prompts span 4 makes the same chunks as span 2 -- the 7K prompt (5,604 tokens) is one interval plus 1,508 tokens either way and the 20K prompt's 10,616 new tokens are 2,624 to the boundary plus one 7,992-token span under both -- so B17 would measure B16 again with 2 GiB less expert residency; 16,384 only differs for prompts past 16K new tokens, which the targets do not name; recorded for the report
decision (run 61, note 50 item 1): the service keeps 4,096-token chunks until B16 measures the span form with the minimum lowered; B15's interval form (`--checkpoint-interval 8192`) is **not** adopted although the 7K first token fell 5 % | alternative: adopt the interval form now on the 7K gain | why: the interval is the linear-state checkpoint grid the prefix reuse keys on -- the 20K prompt that shares the 7K prefix lost its 5,568-token hit and took 70.1 s against 48.7 (a user re-sending a long conversation is the common case; the chunk's +6 % a token does not pay for that); the span form keeps the grid at 4,096 and only needed the scheduler's eight-interval minimum made settable (b3bd92e: an env knob, the shipped rule unchanged when unset)
decision (run 61): :58 is the service image (the unit's digest updated on amd-host and intel-host) on H15's 22 clean requests, although the step ended in the guard's heat stop | alternative: keep :57 until a full 5-minute rotation runs on :58 | why: the stop is the guard's at 75 C after three prefill steps in the same window (H11 on the same setting ran 5 minutes at 74 C when the card started cool), the engine served every request at the expected rates (median 33.2, acceptance 0.69) and :58's only changes are the matrix form's default (measured on :57 under the switch: AG1, B12) and two inert knobs; the next rotation on :58 / :59 extends the evidence
decision (run 60, owner note 49 carried out): the matrix-unit expert form is the service setting -- run.sh exports RADIANCE_XE_MOE_MX=1 on every image, the code default is flipped in the tree (RADIANCE_XE_MOE_MX=0 the GEMV form, one flag away) and committed once a build is allowed, and the default is **not** reverted on the table: the port with the form on agrees with production as often as the GEMV form did or more (identical answers 3 of 11 against 1, tool calls 2 of 3 both times), so the note's "say so plainly" clause does not apply; the one-prompt near-tie (B3flp / prod-7k) is recorded as a known divergence in the report | alternative: keep the measurement on the GEMV form until a build lands, or run the table on :58 next run | why: the form is the same kernel on :57 under the switch, so the table measures the service's numerics now and the owner's order (after the bf16 GEMM, before the GDN port) is kept; the 11 requests were sent once with the logprobs asked for so the gaps are on record (27 of 30 used, 3 left), and the "do not revert on your own" rule leaves the setting the owner's whatever the count
decision (run 60): the agreement table's counts are read like for like with m2's (identical texts of the 7 with text, identical reasoning of the 7 with reasoning, tool calls of 3, fully identical answers), not by the parting word alone (3 requests part earlier than in m2, 3 later or not at all, 5 at the same word) | alternative: the parting words alone (a tie) | why: PROMPT's agreement is semantic (the 11 coherence requests, tool calls by name and arguments), the identical counts are what the m2 report tabulated, and the parting positions are near-ties on 7 of 8 divergences (both sides' margins under 0.4 nat); the eighth (10-tool-event) is the same confident divergence the GEMV form showed in m2 -- a port-wide item for the report, not the expert form's
decision (run 58, stage B's order from the profile): the first token's remaining work is taken by gain over effort -- (1) gemm_nt bf16's matrix-unit form (3.9 s a rank, 12 %; the trunk DPAS kernel's pattern, a day's kernel: this run), (2) the expert matrix form already written (5 s, 16 %; off by default on the production-ranking rule -- the owner's call, restated in the report), (3) the GDN chunk scan port (7.5 s, 23 %; a 614-line HIP kernel on shuffle-emulated WMMA: a joint_matrix rewrite, the largest single item and the largest effort), (4) hc_read_a at M rows (5 s, 15 %), (5) attention's per-row kernel (2.4 s, 7 %) | alternative: the GDN scan first as the largest item, or attention per the owner's note 47 wording | why: the table (B10) is the first attribution the port has had; (1) is a contained kernel with an existing oracle and a known pattern, and the owner's named pieces (attention, the GDN chunk path) are now sized -- the GDN scan is a quarter, attention 7 % -- so the order follows the measured shares, with (3) next once (1) lands; the budget ($392 of $1,000) allows one more large kernel before stage D and the report
decision (run 56, note 47 item 2 closed): cooperative verify is **kept** in the tree (8b9a8bb, 7a31876, 0436e4c, 55c23b8; image :55) as the opt-in it is upstream (RADIANCE_MTP_COUPLED=1); the service's default and the stage D unit leave it off until the owner reads the table, because it changes the sampling law ("fixed-seed tokens are NOT preserved") and does nothing for greedy requests | alternative: revert the four commits (one seed of the single prompt fell on both counts), or set the flag in the unit on the rotation's numbers | why: the owner's rule is "acceptance and tok/s both rise and the logprobs match": on the sampled 11-prompt rotation acceptance rose 0.596 -> 0.668 and the median 28.6 -> 31.0 tok/s (H14 / H14c), the 7K first-token logprobs agree on the top token within 0.01 nat and on the ranking (B6lp / B6lpc; the lower candidates differ by 0.13-0.16 nat, inside the ~0.2-nat band the same arithmetic shows between runs), and the single sampled prompt split by seed (seed 1234 down 8 % / 6 points, seed 4321 up 2 % / 2.5 points) -- the rotation is the owner's user-facing measure and the larger sample; the code is tested (xe_mtp_couple_cpu, the verify on the device) and costs nothing when the flag is unset (M28c on the greedy prompt: 40.2 tok/s, the control's figure)
decision (run 52, stage C closed): no second age value is measured and the mover's policy stays production's for the report; the stage C row reads "the rotation's working set exceeds the resident set: the lever is residency, not the policy" | alternative: mtp4gage256 (the histogram says a 256-step bar would hold 74 % of the readmits) | why: H11h's histogram puts 91 % of the readmits past 16 steps and two thirds between 64 and 1,024 steps -- the prompts' return period -- so an age bar long enough to hold them would serve the same experts as misses instead (PROMPT's rule needs both counts better); the misses (80 a step at 73 % resident, against m2's 8.3 at 87.5 %) follow the resident share, which the tape pool's 4.5 GB a card sets; that is the pool item, parked with its measurement (runs 42-45)
decision (run 51, stage C): the mover's default stays production's policy (RADIANCE_PLACE_MIN_AGE unset) and the stage D unit does not set the flag; the second age value (64) is not measured until the readmit-delay histogram (added to the heat engine's exit banner, image :49) says the bounces are short enough for an age bar to hold | alternative: spend the next window on mtp4gage64 as the run-50 plan said | why: H12 at 16 steps equals H11 on both of PROMPT's counts (misses 79.3 against 76.4 a step, median 31.4 against 30.5; readmits 85.5 % against 87 %), so the readmits are not next-step bounces; with 73 % of the units resident and an 11-prompt rotation the churn is a rotation's period, which no age in steps removes -- residency (the pool item's VRAM) or a longer heat memory are the levers, and the histogram costs no card time because it rides on the traced before rotation (note 48)
decision (run 51): owner note 48's lookup trace rides on a repeat of the "before" rotation (H11t, with RADIANCE_NGRAM_TRACE) and one traced 7K prefill (B5t) in the next card window, after H12 (the "after", already staged and run in this window); the trace is a logging switch in libavx's row_gather (one write a call, off by default) | alternative: build the switch first and trace the before rotation in this window, pushing H12 to the next run | why: note 48 arrived (21:20) after run 50's note read (21:12) and H11 had already run untraced at 21:38; H12 needs no build and is note 47's item 1, the window is open now, and the traced before rotation costs one 7-minute step at the service setting either way (the owner's "no extra card time" assumed the trace existed before the first before run)
decision (run 50, revising run 49's): the matrix-unit expert product (B3, the f16 form) is committed **off by default** (RADIANCE_XE_MOE_MX=1 turns it on; the service and every like-for-like measurement keep the GEMV form v2m) once B4 passes on the card | alternative: default on (30.98 / 55.72 s against 35.90 / 65.28 at 7K / 20K) or not committed at all | why: the oracle shows the matrix form is bit-identical to libref on the tiny model (E7: 1,040 issues, the prefill-shaped ones at rel 0) where the GEMV form deviates (E8: rel up to 0.002), so the kernel is correct and the first-token change (B3flp) is the two arithmetics' difference on a near-tie -- but production ranks that prompt as the GEMV form does (prod-7k), the owner's yardstick is like-for-like agreement with production (notes 40, 44) and a numerics change of the service is the owner's call: the code lands tested, the switch is one environment variable, and the report carries both timings; run 49's "the oracle compared nothing" reading is withdrawn (E8)
decision: a matrix-unit kernel is committed only if the 5,604-token prompt's first-token logprobs stay within ~0.1 nat of the control's for the top candidates (the control: " __" -0.75, "\n\n" -2.08 on :44), on top of the per-op oracle | alternative: commit on the oracle (0.02 a op) and the speed alone, as B2 was | why: B3's bf16 expert product passed 1,040 oracle checks and still moved the first token by ~1 nat (B3lp against B2lp): per-op tolerances compound over 48 layers, and the port's agreement with production is a milestone target; the trunk GEMM (B2) kept the token, which is why it stands
decision: the pool item (the recorded pass's VRAM, target <= 1 GB a card) is parked at its measured state and stage B starts (note 46's order) | alternative: keep iterating kernel variants on K1's spill table (6 minutes a variant) | why: runs 42-45 attributed the +4.5 GB a card to the driver's per-list scratch of spilling kernels (tapes off: flat; kernel objects, list heaps: no; the placement keys: ignored by the driver), and K1/K1b show the GDN update's 32 KB spill does not move with KT, so the next step needs the compiler's spill report or the driver's per-list sizing rule, neither in hand; the floor (6ebd5d8, 1 GiB) keeps the service safe, and the first-token target (47 s against 5 s) is the larger gap. The record for the report: m3/report-pool.md (to write), rows A1-A4, H10, K1, K1b
decision: the io_uring allowance (note 45) does not help, so the default seccomp profile stays in place everywhere (the stage D unit carries no custom profile); the numbers are recorded (I1-I3) and the profile file stays in m3/intel-host/ for the record | alternative: carry the profile for prefill on I2's margin over S5 | why: the same-image control I3 (47.43 / 86.93 s) equals I2 with io_uring (47.25 / 86.62 s), and decode was unchanged (I1: 34.6 / 40.3 against 35.7 / 42.0); I2's -11 % / -8 % against S5 is the image's kernels since milestone 2, not the async table path -- the n-gram reads are not the first token's limit at this prefill rate (the GEMV-shaped prefill passes are, m2 report 5.4)
decision: the no-draft history pass stays issued live (b1c54a1's default) although C9b recorded it without a stall | alternative: lift the stopgap now that the event-only-segment fix holds (C9b: no stall) | why: recorded, it adds a tape per batch width (~22 recordings by the 3-user phase) and the VRAM floor fires a phase earlier (C9b 40.2 / 48.5 at 3 / 6 users against C9's 59.5 / 54.4), for ~15 launches a step saved in steps that draft nothing; the repro result is recorded for the report and the stopgap can go once tapes are smaller (the pool item)
decision: the service keeps `--gpu-headroom-mib 4096` (40.1 / 59.5 at 1 / 3 users); the report's 6-user figure is 73.8 at 6144 (C11), and the kept-tape bound stays at its default (RADIANCE_TAPE_MAX unset) | alternative: 6144 for the service (39.4 / 52.4 / 73.8) or RADIANCE_TAPE_MAX=8 (40.1 / 49.0 / 54.9, C10) | why: stage D's soak is 1-3 users, where 4 GiB wins by 7 tok/s aggregate at 3 (2 GiB more experts on the cards); 6 users is PROMPT's aggregate target (120, out of reach either way) and its best measured figure comes from the larger headroom; the bound only churns the recordings (C10) because a trunk tape is ~0.8 GB -- the per-tape size (the pool target) is the real item, not the count
decision: the service setting is MTP on with the gate (RADIANCE_SPEC_MAX_SEQS=1, hysteresis), `--gpu-headroom-mib 4096` and the history-only pass live, committed after C9; the 6-user figure is re-measured with RADIANCE_TAPE_MAX=8 (C10) before stage D | alternative: MTP off (35.7 / 59.4 / 71.1) under note 42's time-box | why: C9 on :40 is clean (the time-box's condition), beats MTP off alone (40.1 vs 35.7) and matches it at 3 users (59.5 vs 59.4); the 6-user deficit (54.4 vs 71.1) is the VRAM floor sending passes live once 22 tapes fill the headroom, which the tape bound addresses without a build; if C10 does not reach ~70 at 6 users, stage D's soak runs MTP off
decision: PAUSED written at ~13:46 for the denied builds (runs 36 and 37); it was removed by someone else around 14:00 (not by autoresume.sh: no logs/autoresume.log, no logs/PAUSED-* copy), so it is not written again for the same denial (UNATTENDED: a removed pause is not recreated for anything before the removal) | alternative: write it again | why: the removal at 14:00 came with new files (autoresume.sh 13:59:38, units/README-autoresume.txt, ri-autoresume.service/.timer), which reads as someone on amd-host acting on the pause; the next run tries the build again, and a denial then is a new event

On the rotation the split would remove ~80 misses a step at 150-220 us (12-18 ms) while adding a fixed ~10-12 ms of hand-offs plus the host's own compute: break-even to a few percent at best, not the projected +15-25 %, and the single prompt would lose ~29 %. decision (run 76, owner note 61 item 0): phase 1 goes ahead, and the brief's 6(a) is revised down rather than the run stopping | alternative: stop and tell the owner (note 61's stop rule) | why: the rule's condition is "less than ~2.5 GiB of it is memory xe direct would own and free", and the recordings hold 2.74 GiB a card on the single prompt (V2) and 3.6-4.8 GiB on the rotation (H26), all driver list memory (engine allocations +0, no tape-layer device buffers). But the brief's +3 GiB for the experts ignored the first prompt's +1.8 GB of first-use memory (V3: it comes with tapes off), which the headroom must still hold: with the recordings in MBs the headroom can go from 4 GiB to ~2.3 (1.8 first use + 0.5 margin), so ~+1.7 GiB = ~1,440 units -> ~-28 misses a step at H22/H25's slope -> -4.2 to -6.2 ms of the 82.7 ms rotation step -> **+5-8 % (~43.5-45 tok/s), not +10-15 %**; told to the owner in this run's notification, with the first-use 1.8 GB (not yet attributed) as the item that would restore the rest

decision: the next rotation replays run 3 minutes, and the tape bound comes before more headroom | alternative: 5 minutes (H6 stopped at ~2, H7 at ~3.5 minutes of replay, both at 75 C from a 36-38 C start; H5 had lasted 6) or 6 GiB headroom | why: H7 shows headroom only delays the floor (2 GiB more went to more tapes); RADIANCE_TAPE_MAX (6ebd5d8, default kTapes = 24) bounds the tapes' VRAM directly and needs no build
decision: a history pass with no drafting row is issued live (ctx.cpp pass_key, `n_draft_out == 0`; RADIANCE_TAPE_HISTORY_ONLY=1 records it again), and the deadlock behind it stays an open item for the report | alternative: find the deadlock in the tape layer first (C8's all-reduce probe, then the play path's waits) | why: C7 shows the stall needs a recorded history pass; the drafting one (51 segments) recorded fine in every MTP run since M14 and the only new shape under the gate is the history-only one; live it is ~15 launches in steps that do not draft anyway, against 42 -> 32 tok/s alone if every history pass goes live (C7); the root cause is worth a run only if the workaround fails (C9)
decision: the speculation gate stays uncommitted after C5/C6 and the next card step is C7 (history pass live) rather than C6 again | alternative: commit the gate on C5's clean run (6 users 67.7) or rerun C6 unchanged (M11/M12 showed this family is timing-dependent) | why: the gate's code did not stall, but with it the service's useful setting (enough headroom for multi-row recordings) stalls, so the commit would claim a configuration that does not run; C7 both narrows the stall to one tape and, if clean, measures the setting the commit would describe
decision: the service speculates only while one sequence runs (an engine gate to add: draft depth 0 when the step has more than one running sequence) | alternative: MTP on always (single prompt 42.0, rotation 37.5, but 3 users 41.3 / 6 users 49.4 aggregate) or MTP off always (35.7 single, 59.4 / 71.1 aggregate) | why: measured on the same image both ways, MTP wins only alone; under concurrency it is host-bound (C3b/C4) and the adaptive window does not remove it; the gate keeps both best cases. Until the gate is built and measured, stage D's soak at 1-3 users runs MTP off for aggregate and MTP on is the single-user figure
decision: oracle steps on the big model run at 1 CPU (revising "no engine load at 1 CPU" from run 23) | alternative: keep 2 CPUs (O1, O2, O5 all heat-stopped within ~90 s of the load's end: arming the oracle makes the load's end CPU-heavy, O5 read 84 C) | why: H2b's 1-CPU load hang showed the same signature as M21's 2-CPU hang (a thread spinning in libze_intel_gpu after the mover) and both followed a CAT:bcs kill (H2 at 23:18, O2 at 04:42): the stuck blitter queue explains it, not the CPU count; T4 had loaded at 1 CPU in 130 s. Measurement steps stay at 2 CPUs
decision: run 29 goes on after m3 fault 6 (no PAUSED) | alternative: pause under "two faults in one run" (the reset shows on both cards) | why: it is one event (one stop, one reset on both cards in the same second), the forced recovery from m3 fault 5's stuck queue, both keys are reviewed (the runner does not count reviewed faults), the signature has no fix-claimed line, and the cards are clean and present 10 minutes later (checked before the next step)
decision: oracle steps on the big model run with the check cap at 2 a rank (ORACLE_MAX=2) and stop themselves after the first request, so the host reference's load ends before the heat guard acts | alternative: 1 CPU (loads livelock, run 23) or the full check count (O1/O2: Tctl 75 C at 99 s both times, and O2's kill left CAT:bcs artifacts) | why: the decode-shape issues are the first ones checked (O1/O2: 22 of 24 at 1-4 rows), so 4 checks cover the new path, and a step that ends on its own leaves no kill artifact
decision: stage A item 4 (the GDN recurrent update, kernel 4) comes before item 3 (the persistent-kernel exchange) | alternative: PROMPT's order | why: with native tapes the launch-count structure item 3 addressed (~10 ms of the 27 ms step in m2's reading) is already replayed at 0.6 us a launch, the engine issues ~4 collectives a step (ar_calls 864 over 214 steps) at ~0.2 ms, so the exchange's remaining gain is well under PROMPT's 2 ms threshold, while the recurrent update's 296 us x 49 layers (~14 ms a step) is the largest single item of the step and item 4's target (<= 100 us) is worth ~9 ms (27 -> 18 ms, ~55 tok/s single prompt)
decision: no engine load at 1 CPU on images :28+, and the replays run at 2 CPUs in 6-minute pieces with a cool check between (note 16's halving stops at 2 for loads) | alternative: 1 CPU per the ramp, or a longer replay at 2 CPUs | why: at 1 CPU the load livelocks in the driver (H2b: ten minutes, 76 C, a kill with a GT reset); at 2 CPUs the MTP-off replay reaches 75 C after 8 minutes (H2) and every heat stop kills the engine with a kernel-log artifact that trips the fault rules (m3 faults 2, 3, 4); 6 minutes stays below the stop and still measures the memory slope and a rotation median
decision: the service's default is MTP on (provisional until H2 completes at 1 CPU) | alternative: MTP off | why: on the 11-prompt rotation (the owner's user-facing measure) MTP on gives 27.7 tok/s median against 25.7 off (H1 / H2's first 8 minutes, same image and rotation, ttft 1.1 / 1.0 s), while the single warm prompt favours off (36.0 vs 30.6); PROMPT's rotation target (>= 40) is closer with MTP on, and the single-prompt deficit is the open speed item of stage A item 2 (the 77 ms MTP step)
decision: the two-rank collectives launch 32 blocks by default and the backend's immediate list is in-order (image :28) | alternative: keep 64 blocks and test the in-order list alone (an A/B on the residency reading) | why: M13 at 32 blocks is the only clean MTP-on run; the in-order list removes the overlap whatever the cause, 32 blocks cost ~0.5 ms a step at most, and the persistent-kernel exchange (item 3) replaces these launches anyway
decision: m3 fault 2 (card0 fault-response at the T4 kill) gets a reviewed-fault line without a fix-claimed line | alternative: claim be0f1a1 as its fix | why: the signature comes from killing an engine with device commands in flight, which any future `--stop` of a stalled container may repeat; a fix-claimed line would turn that into a pause by the recurrence rule, while the real defect (the deadlock) is already fixed and recorded in T4's row

## Step (stage A item 2 under way): MTP's draft passes under recording
Baseline (run 16, M1 at 2048): native tapes, MTP on: 22.7 tok/s @79 ms, draft acceptance 30.9%; graphs (m2) 9.4 / 10.8%; plain
34.1 / 46%. Method: the engine audits every kept tape (a fresh recording of the same key, compared with the kept one: before the
first play and every kAuditPlays=1024 plays); the backend's diff compared segment counts only. Image :22 makes it byte for
byte on native tapes (kernel object, shape, local memory, by-value argument bytes with the first differing offset, copies), so
a draft-pass kernel whose by-value argument changes between the two recordings fails its audit with the kernel's name and
the byte offset in the step error ("issued differently from its recording ... : <why>").

- Reading of the defect: payload words are stored by 256 threads and the flag by one after a work-group barrier.
  A system-scope release fence orders each thread's own stores, but on the P2P path a peer can see the flag before
  every payload word has landed (more words in flight, more chance).
- **Written: RADIANCE_XE_AR_PROTO=4, the LL form** (NCCL's low-latency protocol).
  - Each payload word travels with the launch's sequence number in one aligned 8-byte uncached store. The reader
    polls each word until the number matches: no flag, no system fence, no ordering assumption.
  - It needs 2 x the message in a parity's slot. The launch falls back to form 0 when it does not fit; decode
    messages fit the band bound.
  - It should fix the divergence and cut the handshake (one PCIe crossing instead of payload + flag + fences).
  - allreduce_test's AR_BOUND_X=k gives the instances k x the message so the LL form runs.
  - Building (l0b), then AB3 = ar-bench.sh 0,4 (correctness first, then the graph-timed exchange).

- **The hc decode is software:** xe_lanes.h emulates v_cvt_pk_f32_fp8 (e4m3_to_f32: ~13 integer / float ops a
  code, exact subnormals and NaN) against one FMA a code -- so the E4M3 dots are ALU-bound, which is why load
  patterns (P31 / P32) did not move them.
- **Level 5 written (uncommitted): RADIANCE_XE_HC_V2=5** = level 4 + (a) `e4m3x4_s8`: an E4M3 code's low seven bits
  << 7 are an FP16 pattern of its value x 2^-8 (normals and subnormals), the sign to bit 15, and the hardware's
  half->float conversion -- ~4 ops a code; the 2^8 goes into the group scale (s x 256 in hc8_dot_down, sc x 256 in
  hc8_dot_up), so every product and sum is the original times an exact power of two: the same bits (the NaN code
  reads +-480, never in quantised weights); (b) hc_v2_down's inject gains with wave_dot_lds<8> (eight 512-byte loads
  in flight, the same order). Instead of the LDS table note 66 named: no bank conflicts, fewer ops. Configs
  svcnomtpl5 / svcmtpl5 / profnomtpl5 (M71's form), kbench V2=0..5, e2e `hcv5`. Building.

## Run 94 (19:50 UTC-): no new owner note -- note 66's hc rewrite
- Settings: firmware 31.1062, boost 1, min_freq 1200, GuC 70.58.0. amd-host pruned by the owner (63 GB free, no build
  leftovers). Boost is still 1, so note 90 item 4's boost-0 proof (and with it the fix as the default and the
  service adoption) still waits.
- Next in note 81 item 2's order: **note 66, the hc decode rewrite** (target hc <= ~4 ms a step from 8.01, MTP off
  >= ~42 tok/s; gates: the tiny model bit-identical or the near-tie rule, M-pair text identical, then speed and a
  rotation).
- The tools:
  - **rad-kbench works on the card for correctness**: `rad-kbench -m <model> --op hc_read --kernels libxe:libref
    --max-ctx 4096 --max-tok 4` checks 30 hc_read cases on the real container's weights against libref in 12 s
    (BK1: 30 / 30, worst rel_l2 1.454e-2).
  - **`--bench` segfaults** right after turning on event timing (BK2, rc 139; the CPU tier's kbench segfault too).
    Speed comes from the engine's tape profiler instead.
- Why hc is slow, from the code: kernel A (hc_read_a) runs ~81 workgroups at one row with ta = 4 columns each, so 4
  of 8 waves stream W_down, after every workgroup re-sums all of h for the norm and stages N in LDS. A bit-identical
  `d` needs one wave a column (the lane-strided sum and wave sum, in order): 320 waves for the card at one row, ~16 %
  of the B70's hardware threads, which is why it is latency-bound. The round-2 probe reached 232 GB/s with 128 lanes
  a column, i.e. a K split, which changes the summation order.
- Step 1, bit-identical (RADIANCE_XE_HC_V2=1, E4M3 rows, decode path):
  - hc_v2_norm (grid hc x rows): kernel A's sum-of-squares order, the scale, N written once to the `u` scratch;
  - hc_v2_down (grid lr/8 + 1): a wave a column, all 8 waves streaming, N from global, no norm prologue;
  - hc_up_mix reads N from that buffer.
  - Image :87 1afff0d4c9d6.
