## Run 92 (17:10 UTC-): owner note 90 -- the pool-in-pieces fix
- Settings: card firmware 31.1062, boost 1, min_freq 1200, GuC 70.58.0, timeslice 1000. PAUSED removed by the
  owner; fault 28 reviewed (note 90).
- Which host allocations exceed 2 GiB (R15's prebind log, 816 allocations): only the two `host_pool`s, 16,991 MiB
  each (kind 3, one a rank). The next largest is 1,546.78 MiB. (The n-gram table at `--ngram-placement ram` would
  be another, 47.68 GiB; the service uses disk.)
- **The fix, behind RADIANCE_HOST_POOL_PIECE_MIB (unset / 0 = one allocation, as before; 2048 = the port's
  setting):**
  - core/mem/pools.{h,cpp}: Pool::init can back a pool with allocations of at most the piece size. reserve() takes
    the first piece it fits and never spans two (a refusal reports the largest piece's room); largest_free(),
    pieces(); the report lists the pieces. Pools::configure reads the variable for `host_pool` only.
  - core/place/mover.{h,cpp}: each class's pinned pool is a list of chunks (consecutive slots, one host-pool
    reservation each, as many slots as the largest free piece holds). pool_ptr() / pool_dptr() resolve a pool
    slot; the 7 `pool_base + slot * stride` sites use them; pool_ranges() reports one range a chunk.
    kXpMaxPools stays 4: its struct goes to a device launch by value. The L0 backend has no expert prefetch, so
    nothing is lost there.
  - Tests: mem_test `a_host_pool_in_pieces_never_spans_a_piece`, `a_host_pool_without_the_switch_is_one_allocation`;
    place_test `a_mover_over_a_host_pool_in_pieces_places_and_swaps_through_chunks`.
  - CPU tests: mem_test, place_test, device_test, hostmem_test pass (l0t). The whole no-GPU tier (l0): 123 of 130
    pass. The 7 failures are not this change's:
    - xe_kernel_props_cpu, images_test, videos_test, kbench, kbench_moe already failed on 10-27;
    - avx_check (libavx lacks moe_host_experts) and ops_doc (docs/OPS.md lacks it) come from b86197b (run 79, the
      host-experts op);
    - trigger_test, failing on 10-27, now passes.
  - **Committed 8674044.** Image :81 65f1c28a441c (HEAD 8674044).
- Card0 had no reset logged after M62's kill (16:56), so card1 first (note 90 item 2):
  - **R17 (17:23, :81, card1 alone, the tiny model): clean**, 64 tokens in 1.67 s, request 2 0.23 s.
  - **HB3 (17:24, :81, xe_hostbind_probe 16.593 1 2048 1 usm: 9 x 2 GiB, card1 only): not a test of the fix.** The
    probe stopped right after its header. At setup it copies its pointer table to every card, card0 included, and
    that copy queued behind card0's stuck job. Its 120 s timeout killed it (rc 124). At 17:25:57 card0 logged
    "Schedule disable failed to respond, guc_id=6", a devcoredump and a GT reset, done: the teardown of M62's
    stuck job (fault 28's queue).

## Run 89 (13:50 UTC-): owner notes 86-87 -- the fix for the two-card bind bug (host allocations in pieces)
- Settings: intel-host rebooted by the owner (~13:40); boost 0, **min_freq 1200 on both cards (arm A, note 87)**,
  GuC 70.58.0, timeslice 1000. PAUSED removed by the owner.
- **decision (run 89): note 87 over note 86's "reproduce R15 once more"** | alternative: one more R15 load for the
  re-armed catcher | why: both notes are from 13:35; note 87 is the owner's, says the catcher is no longer needed and
  forbids binding a host allocation of more than 4 GiB on the importing card, which R15 does (16.6 GiB).
- Where the engine's big host allocation is: Pools::configure's `host_pool` (core/mem/pools.cpp:224), one
  RAD_MEM_HOST_MAPPED allocation a rank (16.59 GiB), a bump allocator. The mover's class pools (~8 GiB a rank),
  the embedding, the checkpoint slots and the staging are sub-ranges of it, and ~20 sites address
  `pool_base + slot * stride`.
- Two candidate fixes, tested first in the probe with every piece at 2 GiB (HB1: 4 GiB binds):
  - usm: separate host USM allocations of at most 2 GiB. Needs the pool and the mover's slot addressing in pieces.
  - import: one contiguous mmap registered with the driver in 2 GiB pieces (NEO's zexDriverImportExternalPointer),
    so each card maps the pages itself and nothing is imported card to card. A device-layer change only (z_alloc),
    if kernels can read such memory zero-copy.
  - xe_hostbind_probe now has both modes, a kernel read check per card, and refuses any piece over 4 GiB
    (note 87). Image :79 b92e7f5458b4; amd-host images :33 and :62 removed (disk 54 GB).
- **HB2 (13:54, :79, both cards, 1 CPU, no model; every piece 2 GiB, card0 then card1):**
  - **a, USM 2 GiB (1 piece): passes.** Copies, and kernel reads correct on both cards.
  - **b, import 2 GiB: copies complete, but the kernels read 0, not 1, on both cards**, and at 13:55:02 both cards
    logged `Engine memory CAT error [18]: class=ccs, guc_id=2 ... in xe_hostbind_pro [10888]` with a devcoredump.
    **A kernel cannot read memory registered with zexDriverImportExternalPointer** on this stack (NEO 26.05): the
    import route cannot carry the zero-copy expert tier. Ruled out.
  - **c, USM 16.6 GiB as 9 pieces of 2 GiB: inconclusive.** All 9 copies on card0 completed (< 1 ms each); card0's
    kernel then never finished (STUCK 20 s). It ran around 13:55:10-11, while card0 was still logging "exec queue
    reset detected" (13:55:11-15) after b's fault. At 13:55:49 card0 logged "Schedule disable failed to respond,
    guc_id=2" (b's faulted queue had guc_id 2) and a GT reset, done. Card1 was never reached. It needs a clean
    rerun alone.
  - **d, import 16.6 GiB: device lost** at card0's kernel. 13:55:53: card0 CAT error class=ccs guc_id 3, an engine
    reset, a timed-out job in [11500]. The same import failure as b.
  - Logs: logs/HB2-hostbind.log, logs/HB2-klog.txt.

## Run 88 (13:10 UTC-): owner notes 84-85 -- the engine-side prebind, and the root EBUSY catcher
- Settings at the run's start: boost 0, GuC 70.58.0, min_freq 2800 on both cards (arm B), timeslice 1000 (note 84;
  arm A still waits for the owner). PAUSED removed by the owner (note 84).

  ~/ri-ebusy/1029T1307). The earlier 1029T1306 folder has an empty ebusy-context.txt.
- Built: `RADIANCE_L0_HOST_PREBIND=1` (off by default). A `host_prebind` hook at the end of the backend table, with
  `rad_host_prebind(stream, tag)` (device.h / dispatch.cpp). In l0.cpp, z_host_prebind copies 64 bytes from every
  host-pinned / host-mapped allocation on the given stream and waits, one at a time, logging each allocation (address,
  size, kind, the card current at allocation) before its copy, and any copy over 50 ms. Engine startup calls it for
  each rank's mover stream, then its compute stream, rank by rank, before the rank and step threads start
  (engine.cpp). Config `svcnomtpoldpb` (m3-tps.sh).
- amd-host disk 57 GB free at the start: removed images :19 and :27.
- Image :77 8d0b0f1219b9 (the tree with the prebind; build l0t 'device': device_test passed).
- **R15 (13:14, :77, both cards, svcnomtpoldpb = R10 + RADIANCE_L0_HOST_PREBIND=1, boost 0, GuC 70.58.0, min_freq
  2800): the prebind names the allocation.**
  - Rank 0 (card0): all 816 host allocations (34.81 GiB) touched in 12.5 ms on its mover stream and 12.2 ms on its
    compute stream.
  - Rank 1 (card1), mover stream: allocation 1 (1,546.78 MiB, kind 1 pinned) fine. **Allocation 2, 16,991 MiB,
    kind 3 (host-mapped: rank 1's expert host pool), allocated with card 1 current, never returns.** The startup
    watchdog's stack is R7's (`Drm::ioctl <- xeVmBind <- ... <- flushBcsTask`); the strace sidecar: 62 x
    `DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND = -1 EBUSY` in 5 s, 78 ms each. 300 s timeout; klog clean.
  - **The owner's catcher did not fire**, though the same 5 s had 62 EBUSY returns. Its bpftrace filter compares
    the raw return register with 18446744073709551600 (-16 as 64 bits), but xe_vm_bind_ioctl returns an int, so
    -16 most likely reads as 4294967280. A filter that matches: `/(int32)retval == -16/`.
- **The reproducer, xe_hostbind_probe** (src/libxe/test/hostbind_probe.cpp, image :78 15de1f5a9b3a). It takes the
  engine's path with no model: sycl::aligned_alloc_host on a context over both cards, then a 64-byte queue::memcpy
  on one card. m3/intel-host/hostbind-matrix.sh runs the cases.
- **HB1 (13:22, :78, both cards, 1 CPU, no model):**
  - 1.5 GiB, card0 then card1: passes. 4 GiB: passes.
  - **8 GiB: card0 binds in 0.9 ms; card1's bind crashed the kernel.** At 13:22:41, `WARNING:
    drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_res_cursor.h:167 at xe_res_next` in `xe_vm_bind_ioctl -> xe_pt_update_ops_prepare ->
    xe_pt_stage_bind -> xe_pt_walk_range`: the resource cursor walking the imported buffer's memory ran off its
    end while building card1's page tables. Then `BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address 0x18` (Oops #1, RIP
    xe_res_next+0x166).
  - At 13:23:02 the probe's other thread oopsed on its way out (Oops #2, `__ww_mutex_lock <- drm_exec_lock_obj <-
    xe_vm_close_and_put <- xe_file_close`): **"Fixing recursive fault but reboot is needed!"**. The probe is a
    zombie with a dead thread stuck in the kernel; the matrix never reached its 16.6 GiB cases.
  - Logs: logs/HB1-oops1-klog.txt, logs/HB1-oops-klog.txt.
- **Reading:** card1 cannot bind host memory of 8 GiB or more that the shared context imported from card0; 4 GiB
  can. With the engine's 16.6 GiB pool the same bind returns EBUSY forever (R10-R15); the probe's 8 GiB took the
  page-table path and crashed in xe_res_next. A threshold between 4 and 8 GiB suggests a 32-bit length overflow in
  how xe walks an imported buffer of more than 4 GiB: a kernel bug to report to Intel.
  - The engine-side fix it names: no host allocation of 4 GiB or more, so the pinned pool comes in pieces.
  - Why it began when boost went off is still not shown. The pool size did not change, so the trigger may be which
    card's import NEO ends up binding at the first step.

  briefs/2026-10-29-intel-xe-import-bind-draft.md (not sent). Image :78 15de1f5a9b3a (:77 + the probe).

  `moe_planes_v2m_kernel<UPL, MT=4>` (sub-group 16, work-group kV2WG) serves a run of up to 4 sorted rows of one
  expert per (n-block, row) work-group: the run's activations staged as f16 pairs in LDS (E4M3 -> f16), the
  expert's 16-level LUT as f16 pairs, each lane streaming 16-byte weight chunks (32 u4 codes) for kV2R output rows;
  per 32-K chunk the products are f16 (level x activation) summed in f32, then `acc += (sum * a_scale[row,

  with `off[e]..off[e+1]` the run, `sorted[i]` the flat (token * top_k + slot) or -1 for padding, `a_sorted` says

  `parts` splits N. The matrix-unit form: a work-group per (64-row block of an expert's run, 64-output n-tile)
  when the run has >= 64 rows (prefill: ~T * top_k / n_expert rows an expert), the leader row's work-group as
  v2m does; stage the block's 64 activation rows as bf16 (E4M3 -> bf16 exact) and, per 64-K group, the 64 weight
  rows dequantised through the LUT to bf16 in the packed B layout; two joint_matrix_mad steps of K=32 (B1's bf16
  32x64x32 -> f32 form: one sub-group per 32 rows x 64 columns, two sub-groups a block) into f32 tiles; store to
  LDS, scale element (row, n) by a_scale[row, g128] * e4m3(scale[n, g64]) into the lane accumulators (the GEMV's
  order per 64-K group; its f16 products become bf16 ones, within the oracle's 0.02), y = acc * scale.1. The

  attention, GDN) are the ones in every segment.

  table refresh points write tables the next kernels read, which at recording time means the host op must run before
  the next segment executes... check ctx.cpp's tape_mark callers for which cuts need device results), and the
  composed blocks could be 64 segments (kBlock) instead of 16 (4x fewer lists a tape; the mover's cuts then compose
  larger partials). Target: <= 1 GB a card over plain for the rotation's shape set, which is also what keeps the
  floor silent at 6 users and on the rotation (the aggregate and the rotation-median targets).
